summary: Four kernel-checkable strengthenings/companions of the sealed Erdos 949 assets, all sorryFree. (1) the 2-fold universal theorem generalized to any AddCommMonoidWithOne (reals inessential) with Z/Q/C instances; (2) the FULL Hindman finite-sums theorem generalized to arbitrary k-fold multiples, recovering the sealed k=2 as a corollary; (3) minimality of the multiplier set {1,2,3,4,5}; plus (4) a refutation that the q<=5 bound does NOT extend to the 3-fold problem (tripling bound is >=9).

open.claim: 3-fold POSITIVE bound: every sum-free S has q in {1..9} with q,2q,3q all outside S (backtracking search finds no counterexample for M>=9; counterexamples exist for M<=8)
open.typed_statement: (k=3, M=9) forall sum-free S subset R, exists q, 1<=q<=9 and (q:R) notin S and (2q:R) notin S and (3q:R) notin S
open.reason: finite core would be decide over 2^27 subsets of {1..27}; infeasible for decide+kernel. Needs a non-brute-force argument.

open.claim: k-fold Hindman over Z/Q (not just R)
open.reason: same proof; skipped as low-marginal-value duplication

novelty_honest: Base problem #949 is flagged 'apparently unrecorded' by the estate. These are strengthenings/companions BUILT ON the sealed formalization, not independent discoveries. The Hindman k-fold result is a standard-style application of Hindman's finite-sums theorem (the novelty is the explicit sum-free-kills-every-nonzero-colour argument and its formal seal, generalizing the estate's own k=2). The finite q<=5 bound, its sharpness, z/q/c generalization, and the multiplier-set minimality appear specific to this formalization. noveltyforge was NOT run; novelty is asserted only relative to the sealed baseline.
